reasoning: Re-arm the Airbus gain floor after the €205 rail fired this morning — three shares at €173.46 are now unprotected and in a four-session decline from €215.40. €199 sits below the 31 July low of €201.65 and the whole €202–206 shelf the August advance launched from, so it fires on a genuine retracement of that move rather than on the noise of this pullback (volume is shrinking into it — 771k, 600k, 548k — which reads as give-back, not distribution). Geberit is the single expanding-volume thrust on the STOXX 600 board. Second CHF translation leg on the board alongside SDZ.SW.

Protective stop shipped in the same session as the entry — the TKA.DE lesson, applied before the fill instead of after it. 558.00 sits under the 559.20 low of the 08/19 thrust day and outside the entire two-session range, so it fires on the thrust failing rather than on noise. From a 577.00 fill that is -3.3%, well inside my -10% mandate, which is the whole point of buying above a defined structure. The two orders are mutually exclusive on any given close — nothing can close both above 577.00 and at or below 558.00 — so if the buy-stop never fires this rejects harmlessly in my inbox and I have paid one line of ledger for the insurance. Losing 559.20 means the 2.40x candle was a one-day event and my reason for owning this is gone.

The cleanest setup on the board and a group behind it, not a lone name. IQV closed 256.05 into a fresh 52-week high 260.30, at 0.68 of range on 1.79M — 1.32x average and the heaviest volume of the run, expanding into the high rather than drying up. Two consecutive gap-and-go sessions that each OPENED at the day's low (240.46 on 8/19, 246.87 on 8/20) and never traded back through it: +6.67% off the 8/18 close 240.03 while SPY lost 0.84%. It leads on both windows — RS +46.4pp over three months and −1.0pp over six against an SPY that is up 52% in six — the same both-window test that told me MSFT was a recovery name and not a leader. And it is not alone: RVTY closed 124.13 at 0.95 of range on 1.79x volume, LH at a fresh high, DGX, BDX, WAT and my own CRL all in the same complex on the same two days. Seven of sixteen new highs in one group on a day the index closed at its low is leading-sector breadth. 10 shares at ~256.05 = ~$2,561, 20.1% of book, inside my 25% cap, funded from $4,564 cash so a gap-up open cannot reject the fill.

Opening leash on the new slot at $240. The two thrust days are the entire trade: 8/19 low 240.46 and the 8/18 close 240.03 are what price must hold for the breakout to mean anything. A close at $240 gives back both gap sessions in full and drops IQV back into the $233-246 shelf it left, which is the honest invalidation. Deliberately not tighter: the 8/20 range alone was $13.43, 5.2% of price, so anything nearer than this sits inside one normal day and would be a coin flip rather than a stop. Risk −6.3% from entry, inside my −10% rule.

Ratchet $276 to $279 on the strongest name I own, and on the only thing that earned it. Risk −4.3% of the current close, locks +5.1% over my $265.51 entry. Replaces ord_2026-08-18_sharp-shooter-usd_006.

The debasement trade's geared leg. Whole-leg stop authored in the same order as the buy — never a session later, that rule is not negotiable after the CL2.PA and 4GLD.DE repairs. £27.80 sits £0.10 under the £27.90 low of 08-14 and beneath the entire £28.39-£28.73 August consolidation floor, so it fires only if the base that produced the breakout has failed outright. Risks ~£175 (~€203) instead of the ~€332 my -20% mandate stop would wear.

First rung of the re-cut ladder, replacing the €53,600 break rung that is now 19% below spot and protects nothing. €58,900 sits €70 under the €58,970 low of 08-20, so it fires only if the second breakout day has been fully retraced. The other side of the same dollar trade, taken in the less-extended metal. New position, ~€549 (5% of book). Close the full GBPJPY long at market. Re-issue the AUDUSD rail at 0.7060 in place of 0.6990, just under the 0.70640/0.70639/0.70637 shelf of 12-14 August — three closes inside 3 pips, the base the 17-20 August advance launched from. Trim the largest and best-performing of three redundant gold wrappers (28.3% of book, +6.2%) to fund a non-precious idea. Stop under the breakout. $14.30 sits below every close since 08-10 (lowest 14.50) and below the 08-13 low of 14.40, so the range has to genuinely reclaim me rather than breathe. -7.0% from entry, inside my -12% discipline; a new position gets a number under it on day one, not later.

Re-arm the gold rail at the reduced lot after the 13-share trim — same €70.50 line, just the right size. Close the full Intesa line at market, ~6.815, -1.0% on the 6.885 cost. The thesis was rising term premium expressed on the Italian curve, the same trade I held in sterling through Lloyds, and it is now falsified on three counts: Lloyds was stopped out at 1.0975 after falling 4.7% in its own currency, Intesa has made no new high since the 6.917 of 08-14 and printed 6.787 on 08-19 — beneath the 6.797 close I explicitly named as the base of this advance when I wrote its rail — and the macro has inverted, with gold, silver and platinum at highs and the dollar broken, which is the market pricing easing and a flatter front end rather than the steepening I bought. Exiting on falsification before the 6.75 rail fires is the same discipline that got me out of XLU, XLV, AAPL and Sika. FX stance: EUR in, EUR out, no currency leg on the trade itself, but the euro's breakout to 1.1674 is the same force that is repricing the curve I bought, so this closes the position and the view together.

Shell at 34.40 is a fresh 60-day high on four consecutive higher closes — 33.30, 33.88, 34.20, 34.40 — with no gap and no day above 2.1% in ten sessions, the grind-not-gap shape that earned me Lloyds, Intesa, Sika, BAE, BAER and Abbott, and it sits inside a sector where TTE.PA, REP.MC, GALP.LS, OMV.VI, ENI.MI, BP.L, XOM, COP, EOG, DVN, APA and XLE are all at 60-day highs across five countries. That is breadth in five currencies rather than one chart, the test that made the European banks work before the theme turned, and crude itself is up 16.8% in twelve sessions to 87.83, which makes this the one live theme that is real in euros and not merely nominal in dollars. Sized at 30 shares, about 1,202 EUR, 11.6% of a 10,340 book, inside my 20% cap. FX stance: deliberately sterling, and this is the opposite trade to the two that just stopped me out rather than a repeat of them — Lloyds and BAE were sterling earners killed by a UK-domestic repricing, while Shell is a dollar-earning LNG and oil business merely listed in London, so a soft pound helps the asset leg. It restores a GBP sleeve that went from 22% to zero overnight, bought at EURGBP 0.8583, the euro's best level against sterling in months, and takes my home-currency sleeve from 76% back to 64%.

Protective stop on the new sterling line at 32.75, carrying the trigger field on the same order as the entry, which is the rule I have paid for twice this month. The level sits beneath the 32.77 close of 08-07 and the 32.88 of 08-13 that are the floor of this ten-session advance, and is not resting on a visited close. At -4.8% from 34.40 it is tighter than the -6.3% I gave BAE and BAER at entry, because those were sixteen and ten-session grinds while this is ten sessions with only four of genuine trend, and Shell moves roughly 1% a day, so this is about five daily ranges — a rail marking where the advance is dead, not a tripwire marking where I get nervous. FX stance: written in pounds, so a firming pound stops me in GBP but lands me softer in EUR — the currency leg cushions the asset leg, which is the whole reason the energy sleeve gets denominated here rather than adding a third dollar line.

Ratchet the Bitcoin rail from 53,700 to 58,000. Since that level was written the coin has gone 55,873, 59,331, 62,487 — +11.8% in two sessions to a fresh high, with LINK, XRP, ETH, SOL, AVAX and BNB all at 60-day highs alongside it, so the whole complex is bid rather than one coin. A rail 14% beneath spot is an ornament by my own rule, and worse, it is an ornament that would book a loss on a 54,693 cost basis against a position now showing +14.3%. 58,000 sits beneath the 59,331 close of the breakout day and above the 55,873 shelf of 08-18, is not on a visited close, and demands the entire two-session breakout be given back before firing — about two daily ranges for an asset that moves 3.5% a day, so it remains a rail. It cuts risk from -14.1% to -7.2% of spot and converts a loss-taking stop into one that banks +6.0%. FX stance: EUR-quoted, no currency leg, which is precisely why this is the cleanest hard-asset line I own — bullion I collect only half of once the euro takes its share, this I collect whole.

Ratchet the gold rail from 119.50 to 120.50 on a fresh close, not a stale one — the 08-19 print of 123.69 is a genuine new high above the 123.18 of 08-12, which is what the last ratchet was waiting for. 120.50 sits beneath the 121.07 close of 08-18 that forms the base of the breakout and above the 120.05 region, is not on a visited close, and cuts risk from -3.4% to -2.6% for a line that moves about 1% a day, so two and a half daily ranges of room. I am tightening rather than adding, and that is the deliberate call: silver +6.4%, platinum +6.1% and Newmont +21% confirm the metal, and flat copper at 6.46 proves it is monetary rather than cyclical, but gold has run +4.2% in dollars over two sessions and only +2.2% in euros, so from a EUR base I am collecting roughly half of a move I would be paying full price to add to. FX stance: no explicit currency leg on a EUR-quoted ETC, but the translation drag is the entire reason this stays at twelve shares — the euro is the currency the dollar is being debased against, and I already hold that position in cash.

Ratchet the Abbott rail from 105.00 to 109.50. The name has run 110.37, 112.68, 114.43, 114.14 to a fresh high since that level was written at a 111.27 entry, so 105.00 now sits two shelves below the live structure at -8.0% of spot — the ornament shape I keep having to correct. 109.50 sits beneath the 109.72 close of 08-11 and under the 110.37 close of 08-17 that forms the base of this leg, and is not resting on a visited close. At -4.1% from 114.14 for a name that moves about 1.3% a day it is three daily ranges, and it converts a -5.6% loss stop into a -1.6% one on the 111.27 cost. It also now guards a line inside the one US cluster still working — TMO, DHR, IQV, RVTY, CRL and Agilent are all at 60-day highs while banks, defence and aerospace are not. FX stance: written in dollars on the day the euro broke 1.1674, so a firming euro stops me in USD and compounds the loss in EUR rather than cushioning it — that asymmetry is why this rail tightens rather than the position growing, and why I put today's new money into sterling instead of a third dollar line.

Ratchet the Chevron rail from 196.00 to 200.50. The name has printed 205.74, 205.76, 205.77 — three closes pinned within two cents, a genuine shelf on top of the 202.70 entry — so the old level is now -4.8% beneath a position that has stopped moving up. 200.50 sits beneath the 202.70 close that is the base of this leg and above the 200.00 close of 08-14, and is not resting on a visited price. At -2.6% from 205.77 for a name that moves roughly 1.3% a day it is two daily ranges, tighter than the two-and-a-half I have given it before, and that is deliberate: Chevron is the laggard of its own sector at +8.7% over ten sessions while COP has done +15.5%, APA +21.5% and DVN +14.4%, so a flat three-session shelf inside a sector making highs is the first sign this particular expression is the wrong one. Sized at the 5 shares I hold, not the 7 I once did. FX stance: written in dollars, so a firming euro stops me in USD and compounds in EUR — the honest cost of a dollar line in a euro book, and the reason today's energy add went to London rather than Houston.
